title: SPHEREx 2025-26 shows unchanged 1,400 K inner dust around ASASSN-24fw; an occulter that covered the star and about 40% of this dust explains its near-infrared light at minimum without a companion
abstract: ASASSN-24fw is an F star at 1.0 kpc. From 2024 September to 2025 May, it became 4.1 mag fainter. Published studies do not agree on its infrared excess, on a companion star and on a star 3 arcsec away. We used data that these studies did not use: 326 SPHEREx DR1 exposures (0.75-5 um, 2025 September to 2026 October, all after the event), 85 ZTF images at minimum light, and NEOWISE and ZTF light curves. We measured forced PSF photometry and a photosphere from 28 field stars of similar colour in the same images. Results: (1) The star recovered completely (ZTF g and r within 0.004 mag of the pre-event level). (2) The 3-5 um excess did not change: 2.52 and 4.96 times the photosphere in the W1 and W2 bands against 2.49 and 5.13 in NEOWISE 2014-2024. The three SPHEREx visits agree to within 4%. (3) The excess starts at 1.5 um (4% at H, 25-28% at Ks). One blackbody fails (chi2 229 for 85 points). An optically thick disc with an inner temperature of 1,381 +- 23 K fits (chi2 94). With WISE W3/W4, 1,045 K + 356 K fits with L_dust/L* = 0.12. A 552 K single-temperature dust fails (chi2 3,553). Thus dust near the sublimation temperature, at about 0.1-0.2 au, makes the near-infrared excess. (4) SPHEREx shows no hydrogen line emission after the event, but the precision is low (6-37 Angstrom). (5) For the published depths at minimum (g to K), a smooth occulter in front of the star plus an uncovered fraction f_u of the SPHEREx hot-dust emission fits all nine bands (chi2 3.3, 6 dof) with f_u = 0.59 +- 0.07. f_u = 0 gives chi2 484. The near-infrared light that is not covered has the J:H:K shape of the hot dust (chi2 2.1), not of an M4V companion (chi2 324). Thus no companion is necessary to explain the shallow near-infrared depths. (6) In ZTF images at minimum, the 3-arcsec star has g = 19.49 and g - r = 0.32 +- 0.05. This is much bluer than a main-sequence star at 1 kpc with the same brightness (about 1.4), so it is probably a background star and not a bound companion. Limitations: SPHEREx did not observe the minimum, so the model assumes that the hot dust did not change; we used the published depths as given; the template and the early SPHEREx calibration add a few percent; the stellar age conflict stays open.
